quizzes.stem: A refund tool meets a slow card service, and each time it answers with the text "Operation failed". The agent tries three more times and then apologises, though a colleague could have settled the case. Which change helps most?

options.a: Reply with the kind of problem, whether another try is useful, and the next step
options.b: Add a line to the prompt that asks the agent to work out which failures deserve another attempt
options.c: Raise the number of automatic attempts from three to ten before the agent gives up on the case
options.d: Return an empty reply so that the agent moves on to its next step without stopping

explanation.a: The agent can only choose a recovery if the reply says which one applies.
explanation.c: Ruled out because more attempts do not help when the reply gives no reason: "Retry every failed call a few times, whatever the reason".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a model with nothing to go on can only guess: "A model that has to guess will retry a request that can never succeed".
explanation.d: Ruled out because an empty success hides the failure: "an empty list marked as a success tells the agent that the search found nothing".

quizzes.stem: A calendar service gets three requests: one asks for a function that it lacks, one gives a date as "next Friday" where a calendar date is needed, and one reaches a backend that answers 503. Which request alone is a protocol error?

options.a: The one that met the busy backend
options.b: The one whose date has the wrong format
options.c: The one that has nowhere to be routed
options.d: All three, because each of them ended in a failure

explanation.c: Only a request with nothing to run is a protocol error; the other two reached the tool.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an input validation failure" is a tool execution error, which the model can repair.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a failed backend call is an "API failure" that comes back with the flag and a message that allows "retry with adjusted parameters".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the specification wants execution errors passed on: "Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction."

quizzes.stem: After a timeout, an agent's wrapper sends the same call again at once. Which call may it repeat without any check first?

options.a: Issuing a refund that carries no idempotency key at all
options.b: Looking up the order record by its order number
options.c: Creating a ticket without any key attached to it
options.d: Emailing the customer a confirmation of the refund

explanation.b: A read changes nothing when it is repeated.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a refund sent twice refunds twice".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "an email that left the outbox cannot be called back".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a ticket created twice is two tickets".

quizzes.stem: A refund call times out, and the tool reports that its outcome is unknown. What should the agent do next?

options.a: Mark the case as resolved, because the service usually processes whatever it receives
options.b: Send the payment again under a fresh key straight away so that it surely goes through
options.c: Tell the customer that the attempt failed and invite them to begin a new request
options.d: Read the records kept for the order, then decide whether any work remains

explanation.d: A write that may have happened is followed by a read.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a new key defeats the protection that a key gives: "The tool sends the same key on every attempt".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the agent would state something unknown as a fact: "the money may have moved, and the agent will say the opposite of what happened".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a guess is not news: "it is the absence of news".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. The billing system refuses a refund because the amount is above the customer's refundable balance. What should the refund tool return?

options.a: A failure marked as transient, with a wait of a few seconds before the next try
options.b: A success whose text mentions the balance, so that the model can decide freely
options.c: A flagged failure not worth repeating, with a sentence to pass on to the shopper
options.d: A failure marked as a validation problem, asking for a smaller number to be tried

explanation.c: A business rule is understood and refused, and the shopper can be told why.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a rule answers the same way every time: "a validation, permission or business failure gives the same answer every time".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the refusal must come back flagged: "a business-rule violation comes back with retriable: false".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the amount was valid and a rule refused it: "The request is understood and refused by a rule".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator delegates to a web search subagent, a document analysis subagent and a synthesis subagent, and it produces a cited report. The web search subagent retries a timeout twice and the service stays down. What should it hand the coordinator?

options.a: A short note that the lookup service was unavailable, sent once every retry is spent
options.b: The kind of failure, the query that ran, any partial findings and other routes to try
options.c: An empty set of results marked as a success, so that the run is never interrupted
options.d: The timeout itself, passed up unhandled so that the whole research workflow ends

explanation.b: The coordinator needs the context to choose a recovery.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a generic status hides what the coordinator needs: "The two opposite mistakes in the guide's sample are the generic status that hides the context".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "an empty list marked as a success tells the agent that the search found nothing".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the other subagents can go on: "a failing subagent must not stop the others".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A wrapper retries any failed tool call twice, and customers are being refunded twice after timeouts. Which change to the wrapper is best?

options.a: Retry nothing at all, so that every failure goes to a person for review
options.b: Retry five times instead of twice, so that fewer timeouts reach the customer
options.c: Retry after a longer fixed pause, so that a late answer arrives before the next call
options.d: Repeat only what is known to be harmless, and report a lost write as unsettled

explanation.d: Only a call known to be harmless is safe to repeat.
explanation.a: Ruled out because many failures do pass on their own: "most failures in a network are transient".
explanation.b: Ruled out because more attempts multiply the duplicates: "a refund sent twice refunds twice".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a pause does not tell whether the first call worked: "A timeout after sending is not a failure of the effect; it is the absence of news".
